summary: Iteration 14 — Backend regression for GET /api/audit scoping fix (root-cause fix for MRF-opening bug). Ran 30 pytest cases against the preview URL covering ALL 22 review-request scenarios (some split into sub-cases for full role-matrix coverage). 28/30 PASSED (93.3%). All entity-scoped audit cases (mrf_/po_/other) work exactly as specified: SE can see own MRF audit, unrelated SE gets 403, PM in project 200, purchase/gm/director/admin unconditional 200, non-existent mrf_/po_ IDs correctly return 404 (not 403), cust_-style IDs allow admin/director/purchase/pm/gm but 403 for SE & store. MRF sanity (PM /api/mrf/<mid>) returns full payload with customer_id/customer_name/items. Audit-filter verification confirms every returned row matches entity_id + entity name filter. The 2 failing cases are the BULK-audit path (admin & director, no entity_id) which return 500 due to a PRE-EXISTING serialization bug: 3 legacy audit_logs entries contain nested MongoDB ObjectId at details.new._id / new_value._id. The current fix's `{"_id": 0}` projection strips only the top-level _id, and FastAPI's jsonable_encoder crashes on the nested ObjectId. Bug pre-dates this iteration (July-2026 fixture inserts of TEST-NEW-1 customer stored the whole insert-response dict) but it now blocks Director from using bulk audit (previously admin-only and equally broken). The scoping-fix behavior itself is 100% correct; only the underlying bulk endpoint has a latent MongoDB-serialization bug that must be fixed separately.

critical.issue: Returns 500 'Internal Server Error' for admin AND director because 3 legacy audit_logs entries contain nested ObjectId at `details.new._id` and `new_value._id`. Projection `{"_id": 0}` at server.py:1998 only strips top-level _id. FastAPI's jsonable_encoder raises `TypeError("'ObjectId' object is not iterable")`. This is not a regression from the scoping fix, but the fix widened access from admin-only to admin+director, so it must be fixed for the bulk view to work. Simplest fix: after `find(...).to_list(...)`, recursively strip ObjectId instances (or `json.loads(bson.json_util.dumps(logs))`). Alternative: clean the 3 offending rows (entity=customer, entity_id=TEST-NEW-1 and similar TEST fixture rows from ~2026-07-16).

rca_of_issue: BUG (unrelated to scoping fix but exposed by it): GET /api/audit (bulk) returns 500 for admin and director. Reproduction: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>' <base>/api/audit` -> 500. Root cause: 3 rows in audit_logs collection (from ~2026-07-16 test-fixture inserts, entity=customer entity_id=TEST-NEW-1 and entity=master.gst) contain nested MongoDB ObjectId at `details.new._id` and `new_value._id`. The endpoint's `find(..., {'_id': 0})` projection strips only the top-level _id; nested ObjectId instances pass through and cause FastAPI's jsonable_encoder to raise `TypeError("'ObjectId' object is not iterable")` while serializing the response list. Entity-scoped audit calls happen to work today because none of the currently-scoped queries hit those 3 rows. Mitigation (either works): (a) sanitize on read — `import bson.json_util; return json.loads(bson.json_util.dumps(logs))` in the audit endpoint, or (b) sanitize at write in the `audit()` helper by stripping `_id` from any dict values in `details`/`old`/`new`, plus a one-off cleanup query on the 3 legacy rows. Recommend (a) for defence-in-depth.
